newsitem.title: USA: CME hogs and pork bellies seen steady to higher.
newsitem.headline: CME hogs and pork bellies seen steady to higher.

text.p: CME hog futures were expected to open steady to up 0.200 cent per lb while pork bellies were called steady to 0.500 cent higher, livestock analysts said.

Firmer cash hog indications as packer demand for cash hogs strengthened should provide early strength in hog futures after futures set a new contract high in July Thursday. Packer cutouts improved late in the week which sparked increased interest in hogs, analysts said.
A higher Japanese yen was also considered bullish to pork as it may increase export demand, sources said.
Further fund rolling could make for uneven trade at times as well as evening of positions ahead of the weekend, they added.

Pork bellies were also seen mostly higher, buoyed by a firmer tone to cash bellies from increased hedger interest and continued light slaughter. The light hog kill this week has resulted in 800,000 lbs less pork belly rpoduction and will likely lead to another out-movement from storage this week, analysts said.
USDA estimated this week's hog slaughter through Thursday at 1,239,000, below 1,294,000 a week ago and 1,344,000 a year ago.
The market is also technically strong after the runup this week and a strong stopper of deliveries should also provide support to spot May, they added.
